why: Part 1: no dashes; same idea
old: "Maya ran 30 feet in 5 seconds" tells you her speed in a useful way. "Maya ran 30 feet" alone doesn't — she could have been racing or strolling. "Maya ran for 5 seconds" alone doesn't — she could have walked or sprinted. You need BOTH numbers.
new:
"Maya ran 30 feet in 5 seconds" tells you her speed. "Maya ran 30 feet" alone doesn't: she could have raced or strolled. "Maya ran for 5 seconds" alone doesn't either. You need BOTH numbers.

Speeds can be huge. A peregrine falcon (a hunting bird) can dive at over 240 miles per hour, faster than a car on the highway.

Try it with race tickets. Some numbers hide under silver scratch panels. Call each race before you scratch.

why: Part 2: “distance ÷ time” in words a 4th grader can use (same meaning, same example); this is what the Slice game does
old: • Different both → compare distance ÷ time. A car going 60 miles in 1 hour is faster than one going 90 miles in 2 hours.
new: • Both different → find how far each one goes in the SAME amount of time. A car that goes 60 miles in 1 hour is faster than one that goes 90 miles in 2 hours (only 45 miles each hour).

why: Part 2: the data table paragraph repeats the list line above it (Part 3 and Part C build the table)
old: A good data table has the OBJECT in column 1, the DISTANCE in column 2, the TIME in column 3, and (if you want) a NOTES column. Then comparing speeds is just looking at the numbers side by side.

why: plain words: “misconception” is a hard word; no dash; adds the wrong idea Bethany ticked (more seconds = faster); leads into the Slice game
old: Common misconception: Some people think the object that goes the longest distance must be the fastest. Not always — you have to check the TIME too. A turtle that walks 10 feet in an hour went farther than a sprinter who runs 5 feet in a second, but the sprinter was MUCH faster.
new:
Watch out: the one that went farther is not always faster. A turtle that walks 10 feet in an hour goes farther than a sprinter who runs 5 feet in one second, but the sprinter is MUCH faster. And more seconds does not mean more speed. Taking LONGER to go the same distance means you were slower.

Now back to Zippy and Scoot. Both of their numbers are different! Slice each run into 10-second pieces and compare the pieces.
